problem: Find a direction vector of the line that is given as the intersection of the planes $z=1$ and $x=y.$
worked_solution:
First, notice that: 

- For the plane $z=1$, a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{1}=⟨0,0,1⟩.$

- For the plane $x=y$ (or $x-y=0$), a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{2}=⟨1,-1,0⟩.$

To find a direction vector for the line, we calculate the cross product of these normal vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & ={n}_{1}\times {n}_{2} \\  & =⟨0,0,1⟩\times ⟨1,-1,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =i+j \\  & =⟨1,1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$
